components.scope: component, store, host-unit, wire, CLI and actual-process row: the knowledge catalog's state export, verified restore and search; operational store migration 23 and the kernel documentation pack store (superseded-only versions, unchanged files, removal only with a later deletion record, append-only deletions, a forward-only head over the state, checks at every open and load); the catalog host serving documentation packs and the ended-run read over authenticated IPC wire 12 with chunked imports; the CLI's --doc-pack-* operations and the harness doc-pack and doc-pack-sample subcommands; the actual CLI and catalog host imported, refused, refreshed, searched, inspected and deleted packs in this sandbox

mutation_checks: run before the source commit with private tooling, each applying one exact replacement and running the package filter: 44 single mutations over the review fixes (route binding, restart marking, the session drop rule, the exact word, the never-stored chain), the knowledge restore and search rules, the kernel store's commit and integrity rules, the host owner's staging, commit, restore and source-reading rules, the catalog host's retention, the CLI's acknowledgments and parsing and the wire bound; 39 made their expected test fail at once. Of the five survivors, two exposed missing tests (state order in the knowledge restore, and two pack operations beside a complete run in the CLI) and were caught after tests were added; one removed a duplicate content-digest check in the store's load, which was deleted because the full-state check covers it; one had mutated the derived export's check instead of the open path, and both sites are now caught, the export by a new test; the regular-file check of the pack reader is an equivalent mutant, because a FIFO is refused by its zero length and a directory by its read. The rerun caught all five. These runs are not retained logs
